These answers show how you talk in footballing terms about the statistical descriptions of a player and involvement.  Later, you are going to be given a statistical description of a player and asked to provide a summary of that player's playing style as it relates to involvement.  It is very important then that you learn to answer, not by simply repeating back the statistical information, but by using the footballing terms you have learned to describe the player.  We will tell you when you have answered enough questions and should start to provide summaries.
Why is expected goals buildup a part of involvement?
Expected goals buildup is included in involvement to give higher importance to offensive actions that are part of attacks leading to shots.
What are the most important metrics for a midfielder?

Ultimately, a midfielder is judged primarily on whether they control the middle section of the pitch or not. If they can move the ball forward through passes into the final third, and/or they can stop the opponent moving the ball forward, then they are doing their job well.
What role might a midfielder who is creative have in the team?
A midfielder who is creative would usually play an attacking role, and would be given licence to move further up the pitch, to play together with the wingers and strikers to create chances.
What skills would a midfielder who is less creative have in order to be considered useful to a team.

A midfielder who is weaker in terms of providing teammates can still contribute to the team if they are strong defensively or in terms of ariel duels. Some midfielders excel in defence, rather than attack. This creates stability for the team.
How is involvement calculated?

Involvement is calculated as the weighted sum of the z-scores of players in aerials (15%), defensive actions (25%), touches (40 %) and expected goals buildup (20%), among other players who play the same position.
If a midfielder is strong in attack (box threat and providing teammates) but does not rank highly in active and  intelligent defence, how do we characterise them?
A midfielder who is strong in attack but not in defence can be described as strong going forward, but at the cost of their defensive duties.
What does it mean for a player to have a low involvement?

Players with a low involvement are not actively engaged in various aspects of the game. Players with low involvement may have limited influence on the match and contribute less to their team's performance.
What are important metrics for assessing a midfielder's ball progressing ability?

We would look at metrics such as progressive passes and passes into the final third, as well as using expected threat (xT) to assess their carries. Ball progression (xT) gives a good overview of these skills. If the central midfielder plays a more advanced role, they may score well for box entries too.
How would you describe a midfielder who is good in almost all metrics?
We could describe a midfielder who is good in all metrics as a well-rounded midfielder, who can contribute to the team both defensively and in attack.
How is involvement measured?
Involvement is a weighted sum of a players performance compared to other players in the same position in aerials (15%), defensive actions (25%), touches (40 %) and expected goals buildup (20%).
How would you describe a midfielder who is not above average in any metrics?
A midfielder who is not above average any metrics could be described as not being a standout in any area.
What qualities do we use to evaluate creativity in midfielders?

A midfielder who provides for their teammates is considered to be creative. These players ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
Is aerial ability important for a central midfielder?

Heading is not the most important part of a central midfielder's role. However, midfielders that are strong in the air can add value to teams by winning aeriald dules in the middle of the field and in set piece situations.
What makes a midfielder strong technically?

A midfielder who is good at providing teammates and progression would be defined as strong technically, demonstrating good technique on the ball. A player who is bad at providing teammates and progression would be defined as poor technically.
What qualities do we use to evaluate a midfielder?
We evaluate midfielders by their involvement, their progression, their ability to provide for teammates, their passing quality, their box threat, their active defence and their intelligent defence.
What qualities do we use to evaluate ball progression in midfielders?

To evaluate ball progression we look at how well they progress the ball with passes and ball carries. We also count playmaking passes, which include progressive passes, smart passes and through passes. We look to see how much danger the midfielder creates through both passes and carrying the ball.
What does it mean for a player to rank poorly in expected goals buildup but highly in touches?

A player who ranks poorly in expected goals buildup but highly in touches is getting on the ball, but not nessecarily getting involved in buildups that result in shots. This can be common in teams who try to build out from the back but struggle to create chances, as their team overall struggles to accumulate xG. So this is not always a fault of the individual player.
Why is it important to have a midfielder with high active defence?
It is important to have a midfielder with high active defence as they will be key in regaining possession of the ball, which prevents the opposition from scoring
How does involvement differ from touches?

The metric touches only considers touches on the ball when in possession, whereas involvement also takes into account defensive actions and aerial duels. Furthermore, involvement rewards actions that are part of attacks that end with shots, but the metric touches values all actions equally.
Does a midfielder progress the ball?
Yes, central midfielders provide an important link between defence and attack, enabling their team to move up the pitch.
What does it mean for a player to rank highly in expected goals buildup and touches, but poorly in defensive actions won?

A player who ranks highly in expected goals buildup and touches, but poorly in defensive actions is more involved in the team's attacking buildup, but likely doesn't contribute much defensively. This can be due to the players strengths and weaknesses, as well as the team's tactics, as perhaps this player is not responsibile to contribute often to winning the ball back if there is another player with the opposite responsibilities.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder is intelligent defensively?

Metrics that measure if a midfielder is intelligent defensively include their frequency of successfully recovering the ball without making an active defensive action or through interceptions. Additionally, a key indicator is their ability to react quickly to the loss of possession and winning back the ball through counterpressing.
How would we describe a player who is less involved in the game?

A player with a low involvement is less engaged in key aspects of the game, possibly contributing less to the team's overall performance and having limited influence on the tempo and structure of the match.
How would we define a box-to-box midfielder?
A box-to-box midfielder is able to cover all areas of the pitch and contribute both in defence and attack. They would measure well in active defence, providing teammates and box threat.
What would lead us to believe that a midfielder is good at creating chances for their teammates?
A midfielder who is good at creating chances would rank highly in providing teammates. They will for instance rank highly in expected goals created with passes and expected assists.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder has box threat?

The key to a midfielder having high box threat is that they get in to the box with the ball and receive the balls in the penalty area. Additionally they should touch the ball alot in the box, score goals and have high expected goal shots.
What makes a midfielder dependable?
A dependable midfielder is a consistent performer in all important aspects of play, regardless of different tactical systems. They are above average over most metrics.
Why are aerials a part of involvement?

Aerial duels can be an important part of a team's playing style, especially for teams that play many long balls. Aerials are not included in the metrics for touches and defensive actions, so they are considered separately to account for them.
Are loose ball recoveries an important metric for midfielders?
Yes, the loose ball recoveries metric demonstrates how frequently a midfielder is in the right place to collect a loose ball. It gives an indication of their anticipation and positioning.
Are linkup-plays important for a midfielder?

Given the definition of link-up plays, they are only counted for attacking players. Thus, they are only relevant for attacking midfielders and do not include plays where deeper midfielders receive the ball from the defenders or the goalkeeper when facing their own goal.
How would we describe a player with numerous touches across different areas of the pitch?
A player with touches across various pitch areas is versatile and heavily involved in the team’s play, contributing to both defensive and offensive phases of the game.
What are the metric which measure if a midfielder is active defensively?

Metrics that measure if a midfielder is active defensively include their frequency of successful defensive actions and their ability to recover possession effectively. Additionally, a key indicator is their high success rate in defensive efforts.
What is a midfielder?

Midfielders play in the middle of the pitch. In attack, they should move the ball from the middle of the pitch to the final third or the box. They should create chances for the wingers and forwards, but also be prepared to run in to the box or shoot when given the opportunity. Defensively, their primary job is to recover the ball in the middle of the pitch and prevent the opposition from building-up or counterattacking.
What does it mean for a player to have a high involvement?

Players with high involvement actively and frequently participate in various aspects of the game. High involvement suggests that the players have significant contributions to their team's performance.
Is dribbling important for a midfielder?

Dribbling is not a key quality of midfielders, but it can be important to more creative, attacking midfielders. Midfielders who are strong dribblers can add value to their team by creating threat out of nothing by dribbling past their markers.
How do we measure if a midfielder provides for their teammates?

A midfielder who provides for their teammates ﻿makes a lot of key passes, assists and second assists. They will rank highly in expected goals created and expected assists. Deep completions are also important.
Are players with low involvement less important to their team?

Players with low involvement are not necessarily less important, but their contributions may be more specific to their roles within the team. For example, strikers who have low involvement but score a lot of goals are often crucial to their teams.
What are the important attributes of a midfielder who has good involvement?
A midfielder is considered to have good involvement if they are active defensively, have lots of touches on the ball and are involved in play leading up to a shot.
What is involvement?

Involvement tells us how involved players are in the game. It takes into account how often they touch the ball, perform defensive actions, and their participation in aerial duels and attacks that lead to shots.
What does it mean for a midfielder to be reliable?
Consistency in progressing the ball, creating for others and active defence are signs of reliability.
Should midfielders who have strong run quality have more attacking or defensive roles?
Midfielders who have a strong run quality are best deployed in attacking roles. They can use their skills to carry the ball up field and make threatening runs in advanced areas.
What are some attributes of a midfielders with a good passing?

Midfielders who have a strong passing ability are able to make various types of dangerous passes. They can cross the ball, progress the ball into the final third and complete passes within the final third.
